Theme

House layout, roofs, rooms & furnishings

hut noun

also cottage, hovel, cabin, shack, cot, shanty

classical

Cic. Tusc. 5.97 (Lewis & Short)
Verg. E. 2.29 (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 5.43 (Lewis & Short)

casa, casae f.

noun, first declension

hut, cottage, cabin

Any simple or poorly built house: a cottage, hut, cabin or shed (Lewis & Short); also the toy house a child builds (Hor. S. 2.3.247). The thatched casa Rōmulī stood on the Capitol (Vitr. 2.1).

Other words

  • tugurium, tuguriī n. — a shepherd’s or peasant’s hut; a hovel

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sest. 93 (Lewis & Short); Verg. E. 1.69 (Lewis & Short)

    From tegō, “cover” (Lewis & Short): a roof and little more.

Examples

  • Potest ex casā vir magnus exīre.

    A great man can come out of a hut.Sen. Ep. 66.3

  • canis parturiēns cum rogāsset alteram ut fētum in ejus tuguriō dēpōneret, facile impetrāvit

    when a dog about to give birth asked another to let her lay her litter in her hut, she easily got her wayPhaedr. 1.19.3–5

See also house, shed, treehouse, a great man can come from a hovel.

SourcesLewis & Short: casa · Lewis & Short: tugurium

Seneca, Epistulae morales 66.3. Phaedrus, Fabulae 1.19.
